challenges.title: One Subject, Three Sizes
challenges.brief: Pick one subject and shoot it wide, medium, and tight from the same spot. Feet planted. Three separate shots, no moving.
challenges.constraint: Do not move your feet between the three shots.
challenges.review: Which of the three actually held attention? Was the tight one tighter than the subject deserves?

challenges.title: Four Corners
challenges.brief: Same subject, same shot, four takes. Put the subject in each corner of the frame. No cropping to fix it.
challenges.constraint: One take per corner, and you may not crop any of them.
challenges.review: Which corner felt least awkward, and what was the frame doing on the other side?

challenges.title: Headroom
challenges.brief: Same subject, five takes. Vary the space above their head from cramped to generous.
challenges.constraint: Keep the head in frame in every take.
challenges.review: At what point did extra headroom stop feeling like empty space and start feeling like intent?

challenges.title: Negative Space
challenges.brief: Put a small subject in a big space. Let the frame breathe. The subject is under 20% of the image.
challenges.constraint: The subject must occupy under a fifth of the frame.
challenges.review: Is there a direction the subject is looking, and did the space agree with it?

challenges.title: Lead Room
challenges.brief: Shoot a person or object that is looking or pointing somewhere. Leave space in front of it.
challenges.constraint: The subject is never centred.
challenges.review: Did the empty space feel like a direction, or just like a gap?

challenges.title: Three Planes
challenges.brief: Find a shot with a foreground element, a subject in the middle, and something readable in the back. All three visible.
challenges.constraint: All three planes must be legible in the final frame.
challenges.review: Which plane is doing the work, and would the shot survive if you lost that one?

challenges.title: Focal Length Honesty
challenges.brief: Shoot the same scene three times: wide, normal, long. Keep the subject the same size if you can, so only the perspective changes.
challenges.constraint: Same subject, three focal lengths, no other changes.
challenges.review: Which focal length lied least about the size of the space?

challenges.title: Shoot Through
challenges.brief: Frame the subject through a doorway, a window, a fence, a gap in something. The obstruction stays visible.
challenges.constraint: The obstruction must stay in frame and not be a full blur.
challenges.review: Did the obstruction add to the shot or just get in its way?

challenges.title: Break the Frame
challenges.brief: Compose so the subject is half out of frame, cut off mid-body. Do it on purpose and make it look designed.
challenges.constraint: The subject is deliberately cut off. No recentring.
challenges.review: Does the cut read as a decision, or as a mistake?

challenges.title: Match Cut
challenges.brief: Shoot two completely different shots that share the same edge or shape. Same position in frame, same size, so they can be cut together.
challenges.constraint: Both shots share a shape in the same place in frame.
challenges.review: Play them back to back without a transition. Does the cut feel earned?

challenges.title: Frame Within a Frame
challenges.brief: Find a doorway, a TV, a mirror, a letterbox. Put the subject inside it and let the outer frame do half the work.
challenges.constraint: The inner frame must be a real object, not a crop.
challenges.review: What does the outer frame add that a crop would have lost?

challenges.title: Parallax
challenges.brief: Slide the camera sideways about 30cm while the subject holds still. The background should shift and the subject should not.
challenges.constraint: One continuous move. No cut, no steadicam, no gimbal smoothing.
challenges.review: Does the background move enough to feel like depth, or did it just wobble?

challenges.title: One Window
challenges.brief: Light a subject with nothing but a single window. Turn off every other light in the room.
challenges.constraint: One window. No artificial light at all.
challenges.review: Which side of the face did you light, and did you notice the colour of the fill?

challenges.title: Practical Only
challenges.brief: Light with whatever is already switched on in the room. A screen, a lamp, an indicator light. Nothing else.
challenges.constraint: Only lights that are already on. You may not switch anything on.
challenges.review: What was the source, and did you hide it or let it in frame?

challenges.title: One Hard Source
challenges.brief: A single bare, small, hard light close to the subject. Let the shadow be ugly and sharp.
challenges.constraint: One source, and it must be hard enough to throw a defined shadow.
challenges.review: How far did the shadow travel, and did you fight it or use it?

challenges.title: Silhouette
challenges.brief: Expose for the background and let the subject go completely dark. The shape has to carry the shot.
challenges.constraint: The subject has no visible detail. Black shape only.
challenges.review: Is the outline readable as a shape, or did it collapse into mush?

challenges.title: Move The Subject
challenges.brief: Same light, same camera, same settings. Move the subject in and out of it across three takes.
challenges.constraint: Nothing changes but the subject's position.
challenges.review: Where was the light most flattering, and can you name what changed?

challenges.title: Split Light
challenges.brief: Light one half of a face and leave the other half in shadow. Cross the line slightly for texture.
challenges.constraint: One side lit, one side dark. No fill on the dark side.
challenges.review: Which side reads first, and does the shadow give the face shape or hide it?

challenges.title: Bounce
challenges.brief: One source aimed at a wall or ceiling. The bounce becomes the actual light. The source stays out of frame.
challenges.constraint: The subject is lit by a reflection, not by the source directly.
challenges.review: How soft did the bounce get, and where did the falloff go?

challenges.title: Same Subject, Two Skies
challenges.brief: Shoot the same subject in two lighting conditions. One with hard sun, one with flat cloud. Keep camera settings locked.
challenges.constraint: Camera settings identical between the two shots.
challenges.review: Which one needed less correction in post, and which one is the better shot?

challenges.title: Motivated Source
challenges.brief: Make it look like the light visible in frame is the light hitting the subject. Same source, or one that reads as the same source.
challenges.constraint: The in-frame source must plausibly be lighting the subject.
challenges.review: Does the logic survive, or did you have to cheat?

challenges.title: Key And Rim, No Fill
challenges.brief: One key, one backlight for the rim, and no fill at all. Accept the darkness on the shadow side.
challenges.constraint: Two sources maximum. Zero fill.
challenges.review: How much of the shadow side survived, and what did the rim separate?

challenges.title: Colour Temperature Fight
challenges.brief: Warm practical against cool ambient. Do not correct it. Shoot the conflict straight.
challenges.constraint: No white balance correction, no gel, no fix in post.
challenges.review: Does the colour clash look deliberate, or does it look like a mistake you did not fix?

challenges.title: Underexpose And Recover
challenges.brief: Shoot two stops under the meter, then bring it back in post. One image, full recovery.
challenges.constraint: Must be recoverable to normal exposure in post with no noise disaster.
challenges.review: How much detail survived in the shadows after the lift?

challenges.title: Locked Off
challenges.brief: Set the camera down and don't touch it. The subject moves through a 30 second static frame.
challenges.constraint: Zero camera movement. If you touch it, start over.
challenges.review: Did the static frame make the subject's movement more legible, or more boring?

challenges.title: Slow Push In
challenges.brief: Move the camera forward toward the subject, slowly, in one continuous take. Nothing else changes.
challenges.constraint: One take, forward only, no stopping and no cut.
challenges.review: Was the push too fast to read as intent, or did it feel like drift?

challenges.title: Tilt Up
challenges.brief: Start framed on the ground. Tilt up to reveal what's above. One take, one movement.
challenges.constraint: Start below the subject. Finish on it.
challenges.review: What did the tilt reveal that justified the movement?

challenges.title: Pan Reveal
challenges.brief: Start on something empty, pan across to the subject. The subject is not visible at the start.
challenges.constraint: The reveal happens inside the take, not across a cut.
challenges.review: Did the pan lead the eye, or did it feel like searching?

challenges.title: Handheld Walk
challenges.brief: Walk alongside a moving subject, handheld, one continuous take. No gimbal, no stabilisation.
challenges.constraint: Handheld only, one take, keep the subject in the same place in frame.
challenges.review: Where did the frame wander, and did the wander read as energy or as drift?

challenges.title: Orbit
challenges.brief: Arc around a still subject, roughly 45 degrees, in one take. The subject does not move.
challenges.constraint: The subject stays completely still. Only you move.
challenges.review: What did the new angle reveal that the start angle hid?

challenges.title: Whip Pan
challenges.brief: Snap the camera from one subject to another on a cue. Keep the blur. Do not smooth it.
challenges.constraint: One snap. No easing at either end.
challenges.review: Was the motion blur readable as speed, or did it just smear the frame?

challenges.title: Pull Back
challenges.brief: Start close on a detail. Pull back until the context appears. One take.
challenges.constraint: The context must only become visible as you pull back.
challenges.review: Did the reveal change the meaning of the first shot, or just widen it?

challenges.title: Fake Crane
challenges.brief: Rise and arc over the subject, like a jib, in one take. Start low and end high.
challenges.constraint: One unbroken move that gains height the whole way.
challenges.review: Is the height gain readable, or does it look like the camera wandered?

challenges.title: Follow Focus
challenges.brief: Frame a subject with something in the foreground. Rack focus from the foreground to the subject mid-shot, while framing stays put.
challenges.constraint: The rack happens inside the shot. The frame does not move.
challenges.review: Did the rack land on the right beat, or did it feel arbitrary?

challenges.title: Drone Reveal
challenges.brief: Fly the Neo up or over a subject so the ground context arrives with it. One flight, no edits.
challenges.constraint: The move must reveal something that was hidden from the ground.
challenges.review: Is there enough texture under the drone, or does the ground read as a blank plane?

challenges.title: Continuity Walk
challenges.brief: A 30 second single take of a subject moving through a space, with no visible seam, no cut, no jump.
challenges.constraint: One take. No cuts hidden inside the move.
challenges.review: Watch it twice. Did you see a seam, and did you miss it the first time?

challenges.title: Thirds
challenges.brief: Place your subject on a third line, horizontally and vertically. Both at once.
challenges.constraint: Subject sits on an intersection of thirds lines.
challenges.review: Did the rule help, or did you want to break it immediately?

challenges.title: Symmetry
challenges.brief: Find an axis of symmetry and shoot dead centre on it. Then shoot off that axis by a small amount.
challenges.constraint: Both shots, same position in the space, only the alignment changes.
challenges.review: Which one felt more deliberate, and why?

challenges.title: Leading Lines
challenges.brief: Find lines in the space that point at your subject. Use all of them.
challenges.constraint: At least two lines must converge on the subject.
challenges.review: Do the lines actually point anywhere, or were you forcing it?

challenges.title: Texture Wall
challenges.brief: Fill the entire frame with a single surface so you cannot tell what the object is. Get close.
challenges.constraint: No horizon, no edges, no context. Surface only.
challenges.review: Does it hold as an abstract image, or does it just look like an accident?

challenges.title: Repetition With A Break
challenges.brief: Frame a row of similar things. One of them is different. Compose so the break is the subject.
challenges.constraint: The odd one out is the compositional anchor.
challenges.review: Did the eye land on the break straight away, or did the pattern swallow it?

challenges.title: One Colour
challenges.brief: Find a frame that is mostly a single colour. Get the subject to work inside that colour, not fight it.
challenges.constraint: One dominant colour across most of the frame.
challenges.review: What is the second colour doing, and is it helping?

challenges.title: Foreground Occlusion
challenges.brief: Shoot past something so a part of the frame is blocked. The subject stays clear.
challenges.constraint: Something is in the near foreground, and it is not fully defocused.
challenges.review: Did the occlusion create depth, or did it just look like a mistake?

challenges.title: Weight Balance
challenges.brief: Two subjects in frame. One heavy and one light. Balance them so the frame doesn't tip.
challenges.constraint: Both subjects are clearly readable.
challenges.review: Which subject is doing the visual work, and is that the one you meant?

challenges.title: Clutter On Purpose
challenges.brief: Fill the frame with visual noise. Make the subject survive anyway. Nothing gets tidied.
challenges.constraint: You may not move, remove, or tidy anything in the scene.
challenges.review: Does the subject still read, and what did the clutter give it?

challenges.title: The Void
challenges.brief: Shoot the space a person or thing just left. The subject is absent. The absence is the subject.
challenges.constraint: The absent subject must be implied by something left behind.
challenges.review: Can you tell what happened without narration?

challenges.title: Break The Rule On Purpose
challenges.brief: Compose something deliberately wrong. Centre a subject that should not be centred, or put it in a corner for no reason.
challenges.constraint: The break must be visible and deliberate, not accidental.
challenges.review: Does the wrongness pull the eye, or does it just look like a bad frame?

challenges.title: Opposing Colour
challenges.brief: Put two complementary colours in the frame and make them argue. Both get equal space.
challenges.constraint: Neither colour is allowed to dominate.
challenges.review: Where did your eye go first, and was that the point?

challenges.title: Before And After
challenges.brief: One object. Shoot it as it is, then change one thing, then shoot it again. Same frame, same light.
challenges.constraint: Identical framing in both shots.
challenges.review: Which single change carried the whole story?

challenges.title: Hands Only
challenges.brief: Shoot a task being done. Hands and the object. No face, no talking.
challenges.constraint: No face enters frame at any point.
challenges.review: Could you tell what was happening, and how?

challenges.title: Arrival
challenges.brief: Shoot a subject entering a space. The space is empty before they arrive.
challenges.constraint: The space is empty in the first shot and occupied in the second.
challenges.review: What did their arrival change about the room?

challenges.title: The Thing They Left
challenges.brief: Shoot the aftermath. The person is gone. The cup, the chair, the cable, the open laptop.
challenges.constraint: No person in either shot.
challenges.review: Does it read as an absence, or just as a still life?

challenges.title: One Clear Action
challenges.brief: Shoot one task from beginning to end. It has to be legible in a single unbroken shot.
challenges.constraint: One take, no cuts, and the action has to be understandable.
challenges.review: Play it to someone who was not there. Did they know what happened?

challenges.title: Cut On A Gesture
challenges.brief: Shoot two shots and cut them on a movement. The cut is hidden inside a hand passing, a head turn, a door.
challenges.constraint: The cut must land inside a motion.
challenges.review: Did you feel the cut, and if so, where?

challenges.title: The Work
challenges.brief: Shoot your actual work. Terminals, hands on a keyboard, a screen, a soldering iron. No face needed.
challenges.constraint: It has to be your real work, not a staged version of it.
challenges.review: Does a stranger learn anything real about how you work?

challenges.title: Sound Off
challenges.brief: Shoot a sequence that tells a story with no dialogue, no music, and no text. Sound optional.
challenges.constraint: No spoken words and no on-screen text.
challenges.review: Mute it. Does it still work?

challenges.title: Five Second Hook
challenges.brief: Open with five seconds that make someone stay. It has to work as the first frame of a longer video.
challenges.constraint: Five seconds maximum. No setup shot before it.
challenges.review: Does it create a question, or is it just a striking image?

challenges.title: Shot And Reverse
challenges.brief: Shoot a conversation with only one side of it. Two angles, no coverage, no reaction shots of the other person.
challenges.constraint: You only shoot one participant, in two framings.
challenges.review: Can you feel the other person's presence in the frame?

challenges.title: Time Compression
challenges.brief: Thirty seconds of real work, condensed into three cuts. The start, the middle, the end.
challenges.constraint: Exactly three shots. Each one from a different position.
challenges.review: Did the middle shot add something, or should it have been two shots?

challenges.title: Room For A Line
challenges.brief: Shoot a composition with deliberate empty space where a voiceover line will go later.
challenges.constraint: The empty space must be in the lower third, sized for a caption.
challenges.review: Is the space genuinely usable, or just empty?

challenges.title: Full Manual
challenges.brief: Shoot one shot with focus, exposure, and white balance all locked manually. Nothing auto.
challenges.constraint: No auto anything, for one take.
challenges.review: Which manual setting did you have to think hardest about?

challenges.title: Pick A Shutter
challenges.brief: Choose one shutter speed and ride it for five shots in different light. Change nothing else.
challenges.constraint: Identical shutter speed across all five shots.
challenges.review: At what point did the shutter become the problem instead of the tool?

challenges.title: Watch White Balance Drift
challenges.brief: Lock white balance and shoot the same scene as the light changes. Watch it move.
challenges.constraint: Manual white balance. No auto.
challenges.review: What did the locked WB do to the colour as the light changed?

challenges.title: One Focus Pull
challenges.brief: Focus on something near, then pull to something far. Do it three times at different speeds.
challenges.constraint: The rack must be smooth and land on the far subject.
challenges.review: Which speed felt deliberate rather than accidental?

challenges.title: Log And Standard
challenges.brief: Shoot the same thing twice, once in log and once standard. Grade them to match and compare.
challenges.constraint: Both shots matched in framing and exposure.
challenges.review: Which file held up better, and what did the log version cost you?

challenges.title: With And Without ND
challenges.brief: Shoot the same shot with an ND filter and without it. The one without will be brighter and shallower.
challenges.constraint: Only the filter changes.
challenges.review: Which one could you actually use, and what broke in the other?

challenges.title: Lock The Frame Rate
challenges.brief: Shoot six shots and put them in a timeline at one frame rate. No auto switching.
challenges.constraint: Every shot at the same frame rate.
challenges.review: Did the frame rate choice suit the movement, or fight it?

challenges.title: Grain In, Grain Out
challenges.brief: Shoot something clean. Add grain in post. Then take it all the way out and compare the two.
challenges.constraint: Both versions exported and compared side by side.
challenges.review: Which one suits the image, and was the clean one actually clean?

challenges.title: Full Auto, No Touching
challenges.brief: Shoot an entire sequence with the camera in full auto. Do not correct anything afterwards either.
challenges.constraint: Zero manual intervention, in camera or in post.
challenges.review: Where did the camera's own decisions outperform yours?

challenges.title: Push To The Limit
challenges.brief: Raise ISO, lower shutter, or open the aperture until the image breaks. Then back off one stop and shoot again.
challenges.constraint: You must break it before you fix it.
challenges.review: What was the actual failure, and would you have caught it without reviewing?

challenges.title: Slow Then Conform
challenges.brief: Shoot at 60fps, then conform the footage to 24fps in the timeline. The motion should slow, not stutter.
challenges.constraint: The conform has to be clean, no duplicated frames showing.
challenges.review: Is the slow motion smooth, and was 60fps the right call for that movement?

challenges.title: One Card, One Battery
challenges.brief: Shoot a full sequence with a single card and a single battery, no spares, no second takes on the card.
challenges.constraint: No backups. If it fails, it failed.
challenges.review: How did the constraint change the way you shot?
